analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by calling `blosc_getitem(coffsets, nchunk, 1, &offset)` on an untrusted/undersized `coffsets` buffer without passing or validating its real compressed size. `blosc_getitem` then invokes `_blosc_getitem` with `srcsize=INT32_MAX`, so bounds checks are effectively bypassed and `blosc_d` performs `sw32_(src)` past the end of the fuzz input-backed heap buffer. Crash manifests in `sw32_` (blosc-private.h:44) during offset extraction, but root cause is unsafe offset decoding in `get_coffset`/frame path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer opens attacker-controlled in-memory frame via `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe(data,size)`, then `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_get_lazychunk`/`get_coffset`. A malformed frame must make `get_coffsets` return a buffer that is not a valid full Blosc chunk (or too short for requested item), while `nchunk` is still considered in-range by frame metadata. Because `get_coffset` uses size-unaware `blosc_getitem`, parsing reads beyond the 89-byte input allocation and crashes.
